conclusion: This benchmark does not demonstrate that Conceptualize preserved correctness while reducing model input or cost. The current runtime pack exposed most history rather than a small delta; one model adopted it and had higher input/lower rubric coverage, while the other did not adopt. The deterministic exact-phrase rubric has wording-sensitive false negatives. No savings claim is supported.
limits: Only two available model IDs and two repetitions per primary condition; exploratory benchmark, not a general estimate.
Every answer failed the frozen strict all-checks rubric; coverage percentages are exact-term checks, not semantic judgments.
The full-history runtime estimate excludes prompt instructions and Codex system/tool framing.
Model-reported input includes Codex orchestration, tool schemas/calls and cached context; not equivalent to raw conversation token size.
Agent-selected context tokens and duplicate savings are N/A because autonomous tool calls returned variable context and the evaluation did not normalize their trace token values to the agent event.
No explicit pricing snapshot was supplied; estimated cost N/A.
MCP latency from persisted traces may not capture stdio/startup overhead; Codex elapsed measures the entire invocation.
Control MCP was disabled by per-run Codex setting; autonomous had only Conceptualize MCP configured.
